arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Smiland argued the 1986 judgment confirms the right to sue in district court.
Mr. Minear argued sovereign immunity bars the suit because the waiver is limited.
Justice Breyer questioned whether the statute allows suits in any court or only the Claims Court.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a specific statute waives sovereign immunity for contract claims in district court. the sides that brought the case argue the 1986 judgment confirms their right to sue there. The government contends the waiver is limited to the Court of Claims.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines where citizens can sue the government for broken water contracts. It clarifies the scope of sovereign immunity waivers. The outcome shapes access to federal courts for contract disputes.
